      <div class="devsite-banner-message">
        <div class="devsite-banner-message-text">
          <p><strong>Firebase Studio is sunsetting on March 22, 2027.</strong> As of June 22, 2026, new workspace creation and user signup are disabled. You can continue to work in and migrate your existing workspaces to Google AI Studio or Google Antigravity. <a href="/docs/studio/migrating-project">Learn how to migrate.</a></p> <p><em>Any apps already deployed to Firebase will continue to run even after the sunset date. Also, all our <u>core Firebase products</u> (like Firestore, Authentication, App Hosting, etc.) are <u>not impacted</u> by the Firebase Studio sunset.</em></p>
        </div>

  <div class="feature-intro-title">
    <h1 itemprop="name" class="devsite-page-title " id="firebase-studio" data-text="         Firebase Studio     " tabindex="-1">
        <div class="heading-text"><span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span></div>
    </h1>
    
  </div>

  <div class="feature-intro block">
    <p class="feature-intro tagline">Rapidly prototype, build, and ship full-stack AI-infused
   apps quickly and efficiently, right from your browser.
  </p>

    
      <div class="video-wrapper">
        <iframe class="devsite-embedded-youtube-video" data-video-id="vVAui3_rvD8"
                
                data-autohide="1" data-showinfo="0" frameborder="0" allowfullscreen>
        </iframe>
      </div>
    
    

<p><span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> is an agentic cloud-based development environment
that helps you build and ship production-quality full-stack AI
apps, including APIs, backends, frontends, mobile, and more.
<span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> unifies
<a href="/docs/studio/idx-is-firebase-studio"><span class="notranslate">Project IDX</span></a> with specialized
AI agents and assistance from <span class="notranslate">Gemini</span>
to provide a collaborative workspace accessible from anywhere,
containing everything you need to develop an application.
If you have existing workspaces, you can continue to work in and deploy them.
However, new workspace creation and user signup are no longer supported.</p>

<div class="button-wrapper">
  <a href="/docs/studio/migrating-project" class="button">Learn how to
  migrate</a>
  <a href="https://studio.firebase.google.com" class="button">Open
  <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span></a>
</div>


  </div>
  
<aside class="preview"><strong>Preview:</strong><span> <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> is in Preview, which means that the product is
not subject to any SLA or deprecation policy and could change in
backwards-incompatible ways.</span></aside>
<h2 id="key-capabilities" data-text="Key capabilities" tabindex="-1">Key capabilities</h2>

<table class="responsive key-functions">
  <tr>
    <td><strong>Import projects from source control, local archive, or Figma
    design</strong></td>
    <td>
      <a href="/docs/studio/get-started-import">Bring your own apps to
      <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span></a>: import a local
      archive, connect a public or private source code repository, or
      generate code from a Figma design and import it with the <a
      href="https://www.builder.io/c/docs/builder-figma-plugin"
      class="external">Builder.io Figma plugin</a>.
    </td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>
      <strong>Quick project setup with built-in templates and samples</strong>
    </td>
    <td>
      <p><span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> provides
      <a href="/docs/studio/get-started-template">extensive framework and
      language support</a> with a large library of
      templates and sample apps, including popular languages like
      Go, Java, .NET, Node.js, and Python Flask, and frameworks like Next.js,
      React, Angular, Vue.js, Android, Flutter, and more.
      Start with a template or sample app from the <a
      href="https://studio.firebase.google.com//templates">template
      gallery</a> and/or create your own <a
      href="/docs/studio/custom-templates">custom template</a> to
      share.</p>
    </td>
  </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>Rapid natural language prototyping</strong></td>
      <td>
       <p> Use <span class="notranslate">Gemini</span> to prototype and
        publish full-stack web applications with <a
        href="/docs/studio/get-started-ai">the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span></a>.
        Generate entire apps with multimodal prompts, including natural
        language, images, drawings. Enhance your app using a gallery of
        stock images from <a href="https://unsplash.com"
        class="external">Unsplash</a>.</p>
        <p>If your app needs a database or authentication,
        the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> sets up <span class="notranslate">Cloud Firestore</span> and
        <span class="notranslate">Firebase Authentication</span>.</p>
        </td>
    </tr>
  <tr>
    <td><strong>Always-available AI assistance from <span class="notranslate">Gemini</span></strong></td>
    <td>
      <p>Use AI coding assistance from <a
      href="/docs/studio/ai-assistance"><span class="notranslate">Gemini</span></a>
      across all development surfaces: interactive chat, code generation,
      tool running, and inline code suggestions.</p>
      <p><a href="/docs/studio/try-gemini"><span class="notranslate">Gemini</span></a> can
      help you write code and documentation, fix bugs, write and run unit
      tests, manage and resolve dependencies, work with Docker containers,
      and more.</p>
    </td>
  </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>
        <strong>Familiar and highly customizable development environment</strong>
      </td>
      <td>
        <p><span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> is built on the popular <span class="notranslate">Code OSS</span>
        project and runs a full
        <a href="https://cloud.google.com/workstations" class="external">virtual
        machine (VM)</a> powered by <span class="notranslate">Google Cloud</span>.</p>
        <p>You can customize almost every aspect of your online development
        environment with <a href="/docs/studio/customize-workspace">Nix</a>,
        including system packages, language tooling, IDE configurations,
        app previews, and IDE configuration&mdash;and share the project and
        its entire development environment configuration with a
        <a href="/docs/studio/custom-templates">custom template</a>.</p>
    </td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td><strong>Built-in tools, emulators, and deployment methods
      with deep Firebase and <span class="notranslate">Google Cloud</span> integration </strong></td>
    <td>
    <p><a href="/docs/studio/preview-apps">Preview your web and Android apps
    right in the browser</a> and take advantage of
    <a href="/docs/studio/debug">built-in runtime services and tools</a>
    for emulation, testing, and debugging.</p>

    <p><span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> seamlessly integrates with
      <a href="/docs/studio/google-integrations">Firebase and
      <span class="notranslate">Google Cloud</span> services</a>. For example, you could use the
      <a href="/docs/emulator-suite"><span class="notranslate">Firebase Local Emulator Suite</span></a> directly
      from <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> to thoroughly test Firebase and
      <span class="notranslate">Google Cloud</span> services like <span class="notranslate">Firebase Authentication</span>, <span class="notranslate">Cloud Functions</span>,
      <span class="notranslate">Cloud Firestore</span>, <span class="notranslate">Cloud Storage</span>, <span class="notranslate">Firebase App Hosting</span>, and
      <span class="notranslate">Firebase Hosting</span> before you
      <a href="/docs/studio/deploy-app">publish your app</a>.
      </p>
      
    </td>
  </tr>
</table>

<h2 id="how-does-it-work" data-text="How does it work?" tabindex="-1">How does it work?</h2>

<p><span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> supports multiple modes to cater to different development
styles:</p>

<ul>
<li><p><strong>Coding with full control</strong>: Work directly in a Code OSS-based IDE where
you can import existing repositories or start new projects, and use extensions
from the <a href="https://open-vsx.org/">Open VSX Registry</a>.
<span class="notranslate">Gemini</span>
provides workspace-aware AI assistance with code completion, code
generation, testing, tool-running, and documentation. You can completely
customize your workspaces, deployment approach, and target runtime
environment with support for extensible configuration using
<a href="https://nixos.org/">Nix</a>.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Prompting without coding: The <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span>, also known as
<span class="notranslate">Prototyper</span></strong> lets you create new workspaces to
prototype and refine app ideas with
<span class="notranslate">Gemini</span>&mdash;without writing any code. Work with the
agent using multimodal prompts to iteratively develop a full-stack app
(currently works for web apps), test and debug, and share your work with
others, right from your browser. You can immediately roll changes back if
needed, add new features, test, publish to <span class="notranslate">Firebase App Hosting</span> and
monitor your app&#39;s performance with built-in observability.</p></li>
</ul>

<p>You can seamlessly transition between coding and prompting to harness the
strengths of each. For example, you can start with a prototype in
the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> that covers the basics, like app structure and
user flow, then switch to
<span class="notranslate">Code</span> to implement more custom logic and integration.</p>

<p>This flexibility lets you iterate quickly and build apps that meet your
specific needs&mdash;all from <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span>.</p>
<aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> The <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> can help you build web apps with Next.js.</span></aside>
<h2 id="pricing" data-text="Pricing, quotas, and limits" tabindex="-1">Pricing, quotas, and limits</h2>

<p>Access to <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> is available at no cost. You can continue to
access and manage your existing workspaces.
Certain integrations (like <span class="notranslate">Firebase App Hosting</span>) may require a
<span class="notranslate">Cloud Billing</span> account.</p>

<p>Learn more at <a href="/docs/studio/pricing">Firebase Studio pricing, quotas, and limits</a>.</p>

<h2 id="governance" data-text="How Firebase Studio uses your data" tabindex="-1">How <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> uses your data</h2>

<p>Your use of <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> is governed by the <a href="https://policies.google.com/terms">Google Terms of
Service</a>.</p>

<p>However, note that your use of generative AI features within
<span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> is governed by the <a href="https://policies.google.com/terms/generative-ai/use-policy">Generative AI Prohibited Use
Policy</a> and the
<a href="https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/terms"><span class=\"notranslate\">Gemini&nbsp;API</span> Additional Terms of
Service</a> (specifically governed by
<a href="https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/terms#unpaid-services"><span class=\"notranslate\">Gemini&nbsp;API</span> Additional Terms of Service: Unpaid
Services</a>).</p>

<p>To block the use of your <em>prompts and responses</em> for model training, do not
use the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span>, and do not use assistance from
<span class="notranslate">Gemini</span> within <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span>. To block the use of
your <em>code</em> for model training, turn off
<a href="/docs/studio/set-up-gemini#adjust-code-complete">code completion</a> and
<a href="/docs/studio/set-up-gemini#adjust-code-indexing">code indexing</a>
in your <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> settings.</p>

<h2 id="next-steps" data-text="Next steps" tabindex="-1">Next steps</h2>

<ul>
<li><a href="/docs/studio/get-started-ai">Start prototyping your new app with <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span></a>.</li>
<li><a href="/docs/studio/get-started-workspace">Learn more about <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> workspaces</a>.</li>
</ul>
